setup: the REAL claude named on purpose (--no-netns --loopback-real --claude ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<v>; the program file read in place, never changed — its sha256 before and after), a scratch HOME and config per variant, FAKE credentials written by the run (sk-ant-oat01-FAKE-A/B), a per-session link CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR=<pool-links/pool-t/sess-1> -> subs/sub-A, every base + HTTPS_PROXY on a loopback mock that records the Authorization header of every /v1/messages request, the strace belt (SIGKILL at the first off-loopback connect); one fresh process per variant
question: at which point after the pool moves a link does a RUNNING claude spend the new credential — the next request, the next turn, or never? (lane readings-attribution-2, P0; the tree said both: usage-pool-engine «a re-point does not reach a RUNNING CLI» and «reaches the running CLI on its NEXT request»)
answer: THE NEXT REQUEST — inside a turn too. midturn: one turn of three requests, the link moved as request 1 landed: request 1 (in flight) A, requests 2 and 3 (65 / 100 ms later) B. midturn-late: request 1's answer held 70 s: requests 2 and 3 (70 076 / 70 112 ms after the move) B. Between turns (3 s and 65 s): the next turn B. baseline (no move): A throughout. 2.1.321 midturn: the same (A, B, B).
